correctness.rationale: The unique indegree-zero source is recognized; stable equitable classes have constant numbers of directed source walks. In a northwest-closed Young diagram those numbers are precisely one nonzero binomial at rank i+j, determining the unordered coordinate pair. In/out equitability forces any off-diagonal transpose-colour coincidence to propagate backwards to (0,1)/(1,0) and forwards along both sides of the diagonal, forcing the entire partition shape to be self-conjugate. This is also sufficient by coordinate-transpose automorphism. Comparing two components, singleton classes give a canonical isomorphism; self-conjugate shapes are recovered directly from the unordered coordinate labels and multiplicities. Both standalone programs were executed and passed their actual finite checks; these are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies every vertex orbit and every isomorphism type, relative to an unbounded natural family of nonrectangular 2D finite posets, by an inexpensive local counting process. It reveals a nontrivial mechanism: root-to-cell binomial paths constrain all stable collisions to transpose pairs, while the complete local boundary propagates asymmetry. In contrast to rectangular products, a Young diagram has arbitrarily many variable steps in its southeast boundary. This all-family rigidity and its exact conjugation exception is structurally meaningful and useful for finite-model classification and canonical comparison.
